  ">

  
    
    
    
    

<p></p>

<p>This document describes how you can use <a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/overview">Gemini Code Assist</a>,
an AI-powered collaborator in your IDE, to help you do the following in VS Code
or IntelliJ and other <a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/supported-languages#supported_ides">supported JetBrains IDEs</a>:</p>

<ul>
<li>Receive guidance to help you solve problems with your code.</li>
<li>Generate code for your project.</li>
<li>Manage the context of your project by specifying files and folders.</li>
<li>Create custom commands and rules.</li>
</ul>

<p>If you&#39;re using <a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/overview#editions-overview">Gemini Code Assist Enterprise</a>, you
can use <a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/code-customization-overview">Code customization</a>,
which lets you get code suggestions based on your organization&#39;s private
codebase directly from Gemini Code Assist Enterprise. Learn
<a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/code-customization">how to configure code customization</a>.</p>

<p>This document is intended for developers of all skill levels. It assumes you
have working knowledge of VS Code or IntelliJ and other supported JetBrains
IDEs, and are familiar with Google Cloud. If you prefer, you can also
explore Gemini Code Assist in
<a href="/code/docs/shell/write-code-gemini">Cloud Shell Editor</a>,
<a href="/workstations/docs/write-code-gemini">Cloud Workstations</a>,
and <a href="https://developer.android.com/studio/gemini/overview">Android Studio</a>.</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> The behaviour of code generation, completion, and transformation are
non-deterministic when used simultaneously with other plugins that either
implement the same shortcuts and/or use the same platform API to process these
actions.</span></aside>
<h2 id="before_you_begin" data-text="Before you begin" tabindex="-1">Before you begin</h2>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><ol>
<li><p><a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/set-up-gemini">Set up Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise</a>,
 if you haven&#39;t already.</p></li>
<li><p>Before testing Gemini Code Assist capabilities in your
code file, make sure your file&#39;s coding language is supported. For more
information on supported coding languages, see
<a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/supported-languages#coding-languages">Supported coding languages</a>.</p></li>
<li><p>If you prefer to use your IDE behind a proxy, see
<a href="https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/setup/network">Network Connections in Visual Studio Code</a>.</p></li>
</ol></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><ol>
<li><p><a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/set-up-gemini">Set up Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise</a>,
 if you haven&#39;t already.</p></li>
<li><p>Before testing Gemini Code Assist capabilities in your
code file, make sure your file&#39;s coding language is supported. For more
information on supported coding languages, see
<a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/supported-languages#coding-languages">Supported coding languages</a>.</p></li>
<li><p>If you prefer to use your IDE behind a proxy, see
<a href="https://www.jetbrains.com/help/idea/settings-http-proxy.html">HTTP Proxy</a>.</p></li>
</ol></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h2 id="chat" data-text="Use the Gemini Code Assist chat to explain your code" tabindex="-1">Use the Gemini Code Assist chat to explain your code</h2>

<p>In this section, you prompt Gemini Code Assist to provide an
explanation of your existing code.</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_1" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><p>To get an explanation of your code, follow these steps:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>Open your code file.</p></li>
<li><p>In the activity bar of your IDE, click
<span class="google-symbols" translate="no">spark</span> <strong>Gemini Code
Assist</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>In the <strong>Gemini Code Assist</strong> pane, enter the prompt <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Explain this code to
me</code> and click <span class="google-symbols" translate="no">send</span>
<strong>Send</strong>.</p>

<p>Gemini Code Assist uses the code in your code file as a
reference to your prompt and responds with an explanation of your code.</p>

<p>To refer to a specific block of code instead of all the code in the file,
you can select the block in your code file and then prompt
Gemini Code Assist.</p></li>
</ol></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_1" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><p>To get an explanation of your code, follow these steps:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>In your IDE, open your code file.</p></li>
<li><p>In the Gemini Code Assist tool window, enter the prompt
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">Explain this code to me</code> and click <strong>Submit</strong>.</p></li>
</ol>

<p>Gemini Code Assist uses the code in your code file as a
reference to your prompt and responds with an explanation of your code.</p>

<p>If you only want an explanation of a certain part of your code, you can select
certain code and then prompt Gemini Code Assist again.
Gemini Code Assist will only use the selected code as a
reference to its generated response.</p>

<p>When Gemini Code Assist provides you with code in its
response, you can select the following options listed at the end of its
response:</p>

<ul>
<li><p><strong>Insert at Cursor</strong>: Inserts the generated code into your current
file at your current cursor position.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Insert in New File</strong>: Opens a new file and inserts the generated
code into the new file.</p>

<p><img src="/static/code/docs/intellij/images/gemini-code-assist-code-actions.png" alt="Gemini lists code actions at the end of a generated code response." class="screenshot"> </p></li>
</ul>

<p>These options are available when Gemini Code Assist identifies
the language used in your code block, and if this language is supported in
your current IDE.</p>

<p><strong>View query history</strong></p>

<p>If you want to re-use your previous prompts, you can find them in your
<strong>Query History</strong> in the <strong>Gemini Code Assist</strong> tool window by clicking
<span class="google-symbols" translate="no">schedule</span> <strong>Show Query
History</strong>.</p>

<p><img src="/static/code/docs/intellij/images/gemini-code-assist-query-history.png" alt="Gemini Query History in the tool window." class="screenshot"> </p></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h3 id="create_multiple_chats" data-text="Create multiple chats" tabindex="-1">Create multiple chats</h3>

<p>You can create multiple chats with Gemini Code Assist which
contain their own context separate from other chats. Your chat history shows
your first chat and the last updated timestamp. There&#39;s a limit of 20 chats.
Once you reach this limit, the oldest chat is automatically deleted when you add
a new chat.</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_2" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><ol>
<li>To add a new chat, click <span class="google-symbols">add</span>
<strong>New Chat</strong> and enter your prompt in the text field. After you enter the
prompt, Gemini Code Assist creates the new chat.</li>
<li>To access your previous chat, click
<span class="google-symbols">history</span> <strong>Resume Previous Chat</strong>. A list
of your chats appear. Select the chat that you want to view.</li>
<li>To delete a chat thread, click <strong>Resume Previous Chat</strong> and then click
<span class="google-symbols">delete</span> <strong>Delete</strong> next to the chat that
you want to delete.</li>
</ol></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_2" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><ol>
<li>To add a new chat, click <span class="google-symbols">add</span>
<strong>New Chat</strong> and enter your prompt in the text field. After you enter the
prompt, Gemini Code Assist creates the new chat.</li>
<li>To access your previous chat, click
<span class="google-symbols">chat_bubble</span> <strong>Recent Chats</strong>. A list of
your chats appear. Select the chat that you want to view.</li>
<li>To delete a chat thread, click <strong>Recent chats</strong> and then click
<span class="google-symbols">delete</span> <strong>Delete</strong> next to the chat that
you want to delete.</li>
</ol></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h3 id="clear_chat_history" data-text="Clear chat history" tabindex="-1">Clear chat history</h3>

<p>Gemini Code Assist uses the chat history for additional context
when responding to your prompts. If your chat history is no longer relevant, you
can <a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/use-gemini-code-assist-chat#clear-chat-history">clear the chat history</a>.</p>

<h2 id="manage_your_chat" data-text="Manage your chat" tabindex="-1">Manage your chat</h2>

<p>You can manage your Gemini Code Assist chat settings by doing the
following:</p>

<h3 id="configure_automatic_scrolling" data-text="Configure automatic scrolling" tabindex="-1">Configure automatic scrolling</h3>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_3" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><p>By default, Gemini Code Assist automatically scrolls through
your chat. To disable this behavior, perform the following tasks:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>Navigate to <strong>Settings</strong> <span aria-label="and then">></span> <strong>Extensions</strong> <span aria-label="and then">></span>
<strong>Gemini Code Assist</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>Search for the <strong>Automatic Scrolling</strong> setting and unselect the checkbox.</p></li>
</ol></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_3" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><p>This feature isn&#39;t supported in Gemini Code Assist for
IntelliJ and other JetBrains IDEs.</p></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h3 id="stop_in-progress_chat" data-text="Stop in-progress chat" tabindex="-1">Stop in-progress chat</h3>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_4" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><p>You can stop an in-progress chat response by pressing
<span class="google-symbols">stop</span> <strong>Stop</strong>:</p>

<p><img src="/static/gemini/images/vscode-stop-chat.png" alt="Button to stop in-progress VS Code Gemini Code Assist chat response" class="screenshot"> </p></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_4" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><p>You can stop an in-progress chat response by pressing
<span class="google-symbols">stop</span> <strong>Stop</strong>:</p>

<p><img src="/static/gemini/images/intellij-stop-chat.png" alt="Button to stop in-progress IntelliJ Gemini Code Assist chat response" class="screenshot"> </p></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h3 id="select-model" data-text="Select the model" tabindex="-1">Select the model</h3>

<p>If you use <a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/overview">Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise</a>,
you can select the model that Gemini Code Assist uses when
processing your prompts.</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_5" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><ol>
<li><p>In the Gemini Code Assist chat pane, click the model
selector dropdown.</p></li>
<li><p>Select the model that you want Gemini Code Assist to use.</p></li>
</ol></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_5" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><ol>
<li><p>In the Gemini Code Assist chat pane, click the model
selector dropdown.</p></li>
<li><p>Select the model that you want Gemini Code Assist to use.</p></li>
</ol></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h3 id="edit_a_prior_prompt" data-text="Edit a prior prompt" tabindex="-1">Edit a prior prompt</h3>

<p>When you edit a prior prompt, Gemini Code Assist regenerates the
response to the edited prompt. To edit your prompt, follow these steps:</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_6" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><ol>
<li><p>In the chat pane, hold your pointer over the prompt that you want to
edit.</p></li>
<li><p>Click <span class="google-symbols">edit</span> <strong>Edit</strong>.</p>

<p><img src="/static/gemini/images/vscode-edit-prompt.png" alt="Modify prompt in VS Code Gemini Code Assist." class="screenshot"> </p></li>
<li><p>Make changes to your prompt and click <strong>Update</strong>.</p>

<p>Gemini Code Assist generates a new response to your
edited prompt.</p></li>
</ol></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_6" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><ol>
<li><p>In the chat pane, hold your pointer over the prompt that you want to
edit.</p></li>
<li><p>Click <span class="google-symbols">edit</span> <strong>Edit</strong>.</p>

<p><img src="/static/gemini/images/intellij-edit-prompt.png" alt="Modify prompt in IntelliJ Gemini Code Assist." class="screenshot"> </p></li>
<li><p>Make changes to your prompt and click <strong>Update</strong>.</p>

<p>Gemini Code Assist generates a new response to your
edited prompt.</p></li>
</ol></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h3 id="regenerate_a_prompt_response" data-text="Regenerate a prompt response" tabindex="-1">Regenerate a prompt response</h3>

<p>If preferred, you can regenerate a different response to your most recent
prompt by following these steps:</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_7" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><p>In the Gemini Code Assist Chat pane, at the bottom of your
most recent response, click <span class="google-symbols">replay</span>
<strong>Regenerate response</strong>.</p>

<p>Gemini Code Assist re-evaluates your recent prompt and
provides a new response.</p></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_7" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><p>In the Gemini Code Assist Chat pane, at the bottom of your
most recent response, click <span class="google-symbols">replay</span>
<strong>Regenerate response</strong>.</p>

<p>Gemini Code Assist re-evaluates your recent prompt and
provides a new response.</p></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h3 id="delete_prompt_and_response_pairs" data-text="Delete prompt and response pairs" tabindex="-1">Delete prompt and response pairs</h3>

<p>To delete your prompt and Gemini Code Assist&#39;s response to that
particular prompt, follow these steps:</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_8" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><ol>
<li><p>In the chat pane, hold your pointer over your prompt that you wish to
remove.</p></li>
<li><p>Click <strong>Delete</strong>.</p>

<p><img src="/static/gemini/images/vscode-delete-prompt-response-pair.png" alt="Delete prompt and response pair in VS Code Gemini Code Assist." class="screenshot"> </p></li>
<li><p>When prompted to confirm if you want to delete the prompt and response
pair, select <strong>Delete</strong>. Otherwise, click <strong>Cancel</strong> to cancel the
operation.</p>

<p>Your prompt and response pair is removed from your chat history with
Gemini Code Assist.</p></li>
</ol></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_8" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><ol>
<li><p>In the chat pane, hold your pointer over your prompt that you wish to
remove.</p></li>
<li><p>Click <strong>Delete</strong>.</p>

<p><img src="/static/gemini/images/intellij-delete-prompt-response-pair.png" alt="Delete prompt and response pair in IntelliJ Gemini Code Assist." class="screenshot"> </p></li>
<li><p>When prompted to confirm if you want to delete the prompt and response
pair, select <strong>Delete</strong>. Otherwise, click <strong>Cancel</strong> to cancel the
operation.</p>

<p>Your prompt and response pair is removed from your chat history with
Gemini Code Assist.</p></li>
</ol></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h3 id="configure_code_preview_pane" data-text="Configure code preview pane" tabindex="-1">Configure code preview pane</h3>

<p>By default, the code preview pane setting for Gemini Code Assist
chat is enabled. With this setting enabled, the preview code block in the
Gemini Code Assist chat shows the first 6 lines of code. You can
expand and collapse code blocks.</p>

<p>To change the default setting, perform the following tasks:</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_9" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><ol>
<li><p>In your IDE, navigate to <strong>Settings</strong> <span aria-label="and then">></span> <strong>Extensions</strong>
<span aria-label="and then">></span> <strong>Gemini Code Assist</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>Search for the <strong>Default Code Block Display</strong> setting.</p></li>
<li><p>Select one of the following options:</p>

<ul>
<li><p><strong>Expanded</strong>: Automatically expands all code blocks in
Gemini Code Assist chat responses.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Preview</strong>: Only shows the first 6 lines of code in the code block. You
must expand the code block in the Gemini Code Assist chat
response to see the rest of the code. This is the default setting.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Collapse</strong>: Automatically collapses all code blocks in
Gemini Code Assist chat responses.</p></li>
</ul>

<p>When the IDE reloads, the new setting takes effect.</p></li>
</ol></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_9" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><p>This feature is the default in IntelliJ Gemini Code Assist
and other JetBrains IDEs and is not configurable.</p></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h2 id="prompt_with_selected_code_using_chat" data-text="Prompt Gemini Code Assist with selected code using chat" tabindex="-1">Prompt Gemini Code Assist with selected code using chat</h2>

<p>Gemini Code Assist can perform tasks or answer your questions
based on the code that you select. To get generated code that&#39;s based on a
prompt with selected code, follow these steps:</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_10" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><ol>
<li><p>In the activity bar, click
<span class="google-symbols" translate="no">spark</span> <strong>Gemini Code
Assist</strong> to open the <strong>Gemini Code Assist</strong> pane.</p></li>
<li><p>In your code file, select a block of code.</p></li>
<li><p>In the <strong>Gemini Code Assist</strong> pane text field, enter a prompt for the
selected code.</p>

<p>For example, select a function in your code and enter the prompt <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Write
a unit test for this function</code>.</p>

<p>Gemini uses your selected code as reference and responds to
your prompt.</p></li>
</ol></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_10" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><ol>
<li><p>In the activity bar, click <span class="google-symbols">spark</span>
<strong>Gemini Code Assist</strong> to open the <strong>Gemini Code Assist</strong> tool window.</p></li>
<li><p>In your code file, select a block of code.</p></li>
<li><p>In the <strong>Gemini Code Assist</strong> tool window text field, enter a prompt for
the selected code.</p>

<p>For example, select a function in your code and enter the prompt <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Write a
unit test for this function.</code></p>

<p>Gemini Code Assist uses your selected code as reference and
responds to your prompt.</p></li>
</ol></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h3 id="add_selected_code_snippets_to_context" data-text="Add selected code snippets to context" tabindex="-1">Add selected code snippets to context</h3>

<p>You can select, attach, and direct Gemini Code Assist to focus on
code snippets. Code snippet selection enables discrete analysis of smaller code
blocks instead of entire files.</p>

<p>When you select a code snippet in your code file,
you can instruct Gemini Code Assist add the code snippet to the
<a href="#manage-context">Context Drawer</a>.</p>

<p>Anything selected in the editor window, but not yet added to the Context Drawer,
is also automatically included in the context. Selected code snippets only show
up for a single chat turn. They won&#39;t persist in the Context Drawer, but remain
in your Gemini Code Assist chat history.</p>

<p>In this section, you add a selected code snippet to your context and get an
explanation about the code snippet from Gemini Code Assist:</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_11" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><ol>
<li><p>In your code file, select a code snippet.</p></li>
<li><p>In the Gemini Code Assist Chat text field, click
<strong>Add to Chat Context</strong>.</p>

<p>Gemini Code Assist adds the selected code snippet to your
Context Drawer.</p></li>
<li><p>In the Gemini Code Assist Chat text field, enter the
prompt <code translate="no" dir="ltr">what does this code do?</code>.</p>

<p>Gemini Code Assist responds to your prompt based on your
selected code snippet in the Context Drawer.</p></li>
</ol></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_11" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><ol>
<li><p>In your code file, select a code snippet.</p></li>
<li><p>Select the <span class="google-symbols" translate="no">spark</span>
Gemini icon and then select <strong>Add Selected Text to Chat
Context</strong> from the menu.</p>

<p>The code snippet is added to your Context Drawer.</p></li>
</ol></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h2 id="prompt_with_selected_terminal_output_using_chat" data-text="Prompt Gemini Code Assist with selected terminal output using chat" tabindex="-1">Prompt Gemini Code Assist with selected terminal output using chat</h2>

<p>Gemini Code Assist can perform tasks or answer your questions
based on selected terminal output. To get an explanation of selected terminal
output, follow these steps:</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_12" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><ol>
<li><p>In your IDE, open your terminal (<strong>View</strong> <span aria-label="and then">></span> <strong>Terminal</strong>).</p></li>
<li><p>Select any terminal output.</p></li>
<li><p>Right-click the selected terminal output and select <strong>Gemini Code Assist:
Add to Chat Context</strong>.</p>

<p>Gemini Code Assist adds your terminal output to the Context
Drawer.</p></li>
<li><p>In the Gemini Code Assist Chat text field, enter the
prompt <code translate="no" dir="ltr">what does this do?</code>.</p>

<p>Gemini Code Assist responds to your prompt based on your
selected terminal output in the Context Drawer.</p></li>
</ol></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_12" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><ol>
<li><p>In the Gemini Code Assist Chat text field, enter
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">@terminal</code>.</p></li>
<li><p>In the list that appears, under <strong>Terminals</strong>, select the terminal that
you want to enquire about.</p>

<p><img src="/static/gemini/images/intellij-select-terminal.png" alt="Select a terminal in IntelliJ." class="screenshot"> </p></li>
<li><p>In the Gemini Code Assist Chat text field, enter the
prompt <code translate="no" dir="ltr">what does this do?</code>.</p>

<p>Gemini Code Assist responds to your prompt based on your
selected terminal output.</p></li>
</ol></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h2 id="specify-context" data-text="Specify files and folders in your workspace context" tabindex="-1">Specify files and folders in your workspace context</h2>

<p>By default, Gemini Code Assist uses the current open file as
context. You can specify files or folders in your workspace for
Gemini Code Assist to use as additional context. When you specify
a folder, Gemini Code Assist uses the files in the folder as well
as the files in subfolders as context.</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> When you include a folder, Gemini Code Assist selects up to
the first 100 files it finds within the folder and its subfolders. If you
require codebase awareness beyond this limit, you may want to consider use of
<a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/code-customization-overview">code customization</a>.</span></aside><div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_13" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><p>To specify files or folders in your chat prompt, type <kbd>@</kbd> and select
the file or folder you want to specify.</p>

<p><img src="/static/gemini/images/vscode-local-codebase-awareness-specify-files-folders.png" alt="Specify files and folders with local codebase awareness for VS Code." class="screenshot"> </p>

<p>To get an explanation on the differences of two files in your codebase, follow
these steps:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>In the activity bar, click
<span class="google-symbols" translate="no">spark</span> <strong>Gemini Code
Assist</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>In the <strong>Gemini Code Assist</strong> pane, enter the prompt <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Explain the
difference between @YOUR_FILE_NAME_1 and @YOUR_FILE_NAME_2</code> and press
<kbd>Enter</kbd> (for Windows and Linux) or <kbd>Return</kbd> (for macOS), or
<kbd>Tab</kbd>. You can also click the name of the file in the list to select
the file. Clicking the file name adds the file to your prompt context and
opens the file in your IDE.</p></li>
</ol>

<p>Gemini Code Assist responds to your prompt while using the
two files you specified for context. Gemini Code Assist also
includes the files you specified in <strong>Context Sources</strong>.</p>

<p>Now that you&#39;ve specified those files, you can continue asking additional
questions or prompts in the same chat history, without having to specify the
files again.</p>

<p>For example: In the <strong>Gemini Code Assist</strong> pane, enter the prompt <code translate="no" dir="ltr">How can I
improve YOUR_FILE_NAME_1?</code> (without the <kbd>@</kbd> symbol) and press
<kbd>Enter</kbd> (for Windows and Linux) or <kbd>Return</kbd> (for macOS).</p>

<p>Gemini Code Assist responds to your enquiry about the file you
specified in your prompt.</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> If you clear your chat history, Gemini Code Assist no
longer uses your files for context and you must re-specify the files in the
chat pane using the <kbd>@</kbd> symbol if you want to make more enquiries
about the files.</span></aside></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_13" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><p>To specify files or folders in your chat prompt, type
<kbd>@</kbd> and select the files or folders you want to specify.</p>

<p><img src="/static/gemini/images/intellij-local-codebase-awareness-specify-files-folders.png" alt="Specify files with local codebase awareness for IntelliJ." class="screenshot"> </p>

<p>To get an explanation on the differences of two files in your codebase, follow
these steps:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>In the activity bar, click
<span class="google-symbols" translate="no">spark</span> <strong>Gemini Code
Assist</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>In the <strong>Gemini Code Assist</strong> pane, enter the prompt <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Explain the
difference between @YOUR_FILE_NAME_1 and @YOUR_FILE_NAME_2</code> and press
<kbd>Enter</kbd> (for Windows and Linux) or <kbd>Return</kbd> (for macOS), or
<kbd>Tab</kbd>. You can also click the name of the file in the list to select
the file. Clicking the file name adds the file to your prompt context and
opens the file in your IDE.</p></li>
</ol>

<p>Gemini Code Assist responds to your prompt while using the
two files you specified for context. Gemini Code Assist also
includes the files you specified in <strong>Context Sources</strong>.</p>

<p>Now that you&#39;ve specified those files, you can continue asking additional
questions or prompts in the same chat history, without having to specify them
again.</p>

<p>For example: In the <strong>Gemini Code Assist</strong> pane, enter the prompt <code translate="no" dir="ltr">How can I
improve YOUR_FILE_NAME_1?</code> (without the <kbd>@</kbd> symbol) and press
<kbd>Enter</kbd> (for Windows and Linux) or <kbd>Return</kbd> (for macOS).</p>

<p>Gemini Code Assist responds to your enquiry about the file you
specified in your prompt.</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> If you clear your chat history, Gemini Code Assist no
longer uses your files for context and you must re-specify the files or
folders in the chat pane using the <kbd>@</kbd> symbol if you want to make
more enquiries about the files.</span></aside></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h3 id="manage-context" data-text="Manage files and folders in the Context Drawer" tabindex="-1">Manage files and folders in the Context Drawer</h3>

<p>After you <a href="#specify-context">specify a file or folder to be used as context for your Gemini Code Assist prompts</a>, these files and folders
are placed in the <em>Context Drawer</em>, where you can view and remove them from the
prompt context.</p>

<p>To manage the files and folders in your Context Drawer, perform the following
tasks:</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_14" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Chats created with Gemini Code Assist for VS Code, prior
to version <code translate="no" dir="ltr">2.34.0</code>, won&#39;t retain and display the saved context in the Context
Drawer. This can lead to issues where the chat doesn&#39;t display the correct
context. To build and retain context among chats, we recommend you clear chats
prior to this version.</span></aside>
<ol>
<li><p>In the activity bar of your IDE, click
<span class="google-symbols" translate="no">spark</span> <strong>Gemini Code
Assist</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>To view the files and folders in your Context Drawer, click <strong>Context
items</strong>.</p>

<p><img src="/static/gemini/images/vscode-context-drawer.png" alt="Context Drawer for Gemini Code Assist for VS Code" class="screenshot"> </p></li>
<li><p>To remove items from the Context Drawer, click
<span class="google-symbols" translate="no">close</span> <strong>Remove</strong>.</p></li>
</ol></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_14" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><ol>
<li><p>In the activity bar, click
<span class="google-symbols" translate="no">spark</span> <strong>Gemini Code
Assist.</strong></p></li>
<li><p>To view the files and folders in your Context Drawer, click <strong>Context</strong>.</p>

<p><img src="/static/gemini/images/intellij-context-drawer.png" alt="Context Drawer for Gemini Code Assist for IntelliJ" class="screenshot"> </p></li>
<li><p>To remove files and folders from the Context Drawer, click
<span class="google-symbols" translate="no">close</span> <strong>Remove</strong>.</p></li>
</ol></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h2 id="exclude_files_from_local_context" data-text="Exclude files from local context" tabindex="-1">Exclude files from local context</h2>

<p>If files are specified in a <code translate="no" dir="ltr">.aiexclude</code> or <code translate="no" dir="ltr">.gitignore</code> file,
Gemini Code Assist by default excludes them from local use in the
context for code completion, code generation, code transformation, and chat.</p>

<p>To learn how to exclude files from local use, see
<a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/create-aiexclude-file">Exclude files from Gemini Code Assist use</a>.</p>

<h2 id="revert_to_a_checkpoint_in_chat" data-text="Revert to a checkpoint in chat" tabindex="-1">Revert to a checkpoint in chat</h2>

<p>After applying the changes that Gemini Code Assist generates
based on your prompt, you can choose to revert the modified code file(s) to a
certain checkpoint, which reverts all of the applied changes to the code
file(s).</p>

<p>Reverting to a checkpoint does <em>not</em> revert manual changes that you may have
made to the code file(s).</p>

<p>To revert your code file to a checkpoint, follow these steps:</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_15" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><p>In the Gemini Code Assist chat pane, click
<span class="google-symbols">undo</span> <strong>Revert to checkpoint</strong>. This
reverts your code file back to the checkpoint state before the edits were
made.</p></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_15" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><p>If you&#39;ve already clicked <span class="google-symbols">check</span> <strong>Accept
changes</strong> for a chat generated code suggestion, then you have the option to
rollback the changes using the <span class="google-symbols">undo</span>
<strong>Rollback changes</strong> button:</p>

<p>In the Gemini Code Assist chat pane, click
<span class="google-symbols">undo</span> <strong>Rollback Changes</strong>. This reverts
your code file back to the checkpoint state before the edits were made.</p>

<p><img src="/static/gemini/images/intellij-revert-to-checkpoint.png" alt="Revert to checkpoint button in IntelliJ Gemini Code Assist."></p></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h2 id="view_code_diffs" data-text="View code diffs" tabindex="-1">View code diffs</h2>

<p>By default, Gemini Code Assist suggests changes to your code with
a code diff. You can trigger this diff any time you ask
Gemini Code Assist to make changes to your code.</p>

<p>In this section, you prompt Gemini Code Assist to optimize your
code file, view the diff in your code file, and accept or reject changes as
preferred.</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_16" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><ol>
<li><p>With your code file opened, prompt Gemini Code Assist to
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">optimize this file</code>. If you want to optimize multiple files and folders,
prompt Gemini Code Assist to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">optimize @FILE1 and @FILE2</code>.</p>

<p>Gemini Code Assist responds to your prompt with code change
suggestions in the code file(s) along with an inline diff that illustrates
these changes.</p></li>
<li><p>In the code file, click
<span class="google-symbols">check_small</span> <strong>Accept</strong> or
<span class="google-symbols">close_small</span> <strong>Reject</strong>.</p>

<p><img src="/static/gemini/images/vscode-accept-reject-diff.png" alt="Accept or reject suggested a single change in a file in VS Code Gemini Code Assist." class="screenshot"> </p></li>
<li><p>If Gemini Code Assist suggests multiple changes throughout
your code file(s), click <strong>View</strong> above the suggestion and then click
<strong>Next</strong> or <strong>Previous</strong>, to cycles through the other suggestions.</p></li>
<li><p>If you want to accept or reject all of the suggested changes, click
<strong>Accept file</strong> or <strong>Reject file</strong>.</p>

<p><img src="/static/gemini/images/vscode-accept-reject-file.png" alt="Accept or reject all changes in a file in VS Code Gemini Code Assist." class="screenshot"> </p></li>
<li><p>You can also use the Quick Preview in the prompt response to accept or
reject all suggestions across multiple code files.</p>

<p><img src="/static/gemini/images/vscode-quick-preview.png" alt="Quick Preview in VS Code Gemini Code Assist." class="screenshot"> </p></li>
</ol></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_16" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><ol>
<li><p>With your code file opened, prompt Gemini Code Assist to
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">optimize this file</code>. If you want to optimize multiple files and
folders prompt Gemini Code Assist to
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">optimize @FILE1 and @FILE2</code>.</p>

<p>Gemini Code Assist responds to your prompt with code
change suggestions in the code file(s) along with an inline diff that
illustrates these changes.</p></li>
<li><p>In the code file, click
<span class="google-symbols">check_small</span> <strong>Accept</strong> or
<span class="google-symbols">undo</span> <strong>Reject</strong>.</p>

<p><img src="/static/gemini/images/intellij-accept-reject-diff.png" alt="Accept or reject suggested a single change in a file in IntelliJ Gemini Code Assist." class="screenshot"> </p></li>
<li><p>If Gemini Code Assist suggests multiple changes throughout
your code file(s), click
<span class="google-symbols">arrow_upward</span> or
<span class="google-symbols">arrow_downward</span> to cycle
through the other suggestions.</p>

<p><img src="/static/gemini/images/intellij-cycle-diffs.png" alt="Cycle through changes in a file in IntelliJ Code Gemini Code Assist." class="screenshot"> </p></li>
<li><p>You can also use the Quick Preview in the prompt response to accept or
reject all suggestions across multiple code files.</p>

<p><img src="/static/gemini/images/intellij-quick-preview.png" alt="Quick Preview in IntelliJ Code Gemini Code Assist." class="screenshot"> </p></li>
</ol></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h3 id="change_diff_view_settings" data-text="Change diff view settings" tabindex="-1">Change diff view settings</h3>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_17" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><p>If you prefer, you can change this setting to have a separate diff view
 window in your IDE by following these steps:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>In the activity bar, navigate to
<span class="google-symbols">settings</span> <strong>Settings</strong> <span aria-label="and then">></span>
<strong>Settings</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>In the <strong>User</strong> tab of the settings, navigate to <strong>Extensions</strong>
<span aria-label="and then">></span> <strong>Gemini Code Assist</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>Scroll to the <strong>Geminicodeassist &gt; Chat: Change View</strong> setting.</p></li>
<li><p>In the dropdown list, select one of the following options:</p>

<ul>
<li><p><strong>Inline suggestions</strong> (enabled by default): Code changes displayed in
your code file.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Default diff view</strong>: Opens a new file with side-by-side code
changes.</p></li>
</ul></li>
</ol></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_17" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><ol>
<li><p>In the chat response of the Gemini Code Assist sidebar Ask
panel, click the <strong>Preview in diff mode</strong> button
(<span class="google-symbols">compare_arrows</span>).</p>

<p>A <strong>Side-by-side</strong> tab appears in the main coding pane.</p></li>
<li><p>Click on the <strong>Side-by-side</strong> tab to view side-by-side code changes.</p></li>
</ol></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h2 id="outline" data-text="Generate and view a file outline" tabindex="-1">Generate and view a file outline</h2>

<p>By default, Gemini Code Assist generates an outline for the file
in focus in your IDE. Note that outlines don&#39;t persist between IDE sessions,
which means a new outline is generated for a given file when you start a new
session, unless you <a href="#outline-settings">disable automatic outline generation</a>.
To view the outline generated by Gemini Code Assist, do the
following:</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_18" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><ol>
<li><p>In the Explorer sidebar, click the
<strong>Gemini Code Assist outline</strong> icon.</p>

<p>The Gemini Code Assist outline pane opens.</p></li>
<li><p>By default, the outline pane automatically generates an outline for the
current file in focus.</p>

<ul>
<li>If you previously
<a href="#outline-settings">disabled automatic outline generation</a>, click
the <strong>Generate outline</strong> button to generate an outline for the current
file in focus.</li>
</ul></li>
<li><p>(Optional): Click on a node in the outline to automatically
scroll to that portion of the code file.</p></li>
<li><p>(Optional): Click the <strong>Eye</strong> icon in the outline pane to
display the outline in-line in the code file itself.</p></li>
</ol>

<p>When you make changes to a file that has an outline, a new outline is not
automatically generated. Instead, an <strong>Obsolete</strong> banner appears at the
bottom of the outline with an option to manually <strong>Refresh</strong> the outline.</p></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_18" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><ol>
<li><p>In the Gemini Code Assist chat pane, click the <strong>Outline</strong>
tab.</p>

<p>The outline for the active file appears in the tab.</p></li>
<li><p>(Optional): Click the <strong>Eye</strong> icon associated with the file outline to
display the outline in-line in the code file itself.</p></li>
<li><p>(Optional): Click the <strong>Eye</strong> icon that appears next to the <strong>Outline</strong>
tab to display all available outlines in-line in their respective code
files.</p></li>
</ol>

<p>When you make changes to a file that has an outline, a new outline is not
automatically generated. Instead, the option to manually <strong>Refresh outline</strong>
becomes available in the <strong>Outline</strong> tab.</p></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h3 id="outline-settings" data-text="Toggle automatic outline generation" tabindex="-1">Toggle automatic outline generation</h3>

<p>To toggle automatic Gemini Code Assist outline generation of
your code files, do the following:</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_19" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><ol>
<li><p>Navigate to <strong>Settings</strong> <span aria-label="and then">></span> <strong>User</strong> <span aria-label="and then">></span>
<strong>Extensions</strong> <span aria-label="and then">></span> <strong>Gemini Code Assist</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>In the <strong>Gemini Code Assist</strong> window, toggle
<strong>Outlines: Automatic Outline Generation</strong>.</p></li>
</ol>

<p>If you disable automatic outline generation, you can manually generate an
outline for the file in focus by right-clicking in the file and selecting
<strong>Gemini Code Assist</strong> <span aria-label="and then">></span> <strong>Outline current file</strong>,
or by going to the <strong>Gemini Code Assist outline</strong> pane and
clicking the <strong>Generate outline</strong> button.</p></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_19" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><ol>
<li><p>In your IDE, navigate to <strong>Settings</strong> <span aria-label="and then">></span> <strong>Tools</strong> <span aria-label="and then">></span>
<strong>Gemini</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>In the <strong>Gemini settings</strong> window, toggle
<strong>Enable automatic outline generation</strong>.</p></li>
</ol>

<p>If you disable automatic outline generation, you can manually generate an
outline for the file in focus by going to the <strong>Outline</strong> tab and
clicking <strong>Generate Outline</strong>.</p></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h2 id="create_custom_commands" data-text="Create custom commands" tabindex="-1">Create custom commands</h2>

<p>By default, Gemini Code Assist provides commands like
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">/generate</code> for VS Code and <strong>Generate Code</strong> for IntelliJ and
<a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/supported-languages#supported_ides">other supported JetBrains IDEs</a>. You can also create your own
custom commands to help you accomplish repetitive tasks faster in your IDE.</p>

<p>In this section, you create a custom command called <code translate="no" dir="ltr">add-comments</code> that adds
comments to the code in your code file. For IntelliJ and other supported
JetBrains IDEs, you&#39;ll create, save, and execute the custom command from the
Prompt Library, and from the in-editor prompt.</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_20" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><ol>
<li><p>In your code file, press <kbd>Control+I</kbd> (for Windows and Linux) or
<kbd>Command+I</kbd> (for macOS) to open the
<strong>Gemini Code Assist Quick Pick</strong> menu.</p></li>
<li><p>In the menu, search for and select <strong>Preferences: Open Settings (UI)</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>In the <strong>Search settings</strong> field, enter <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Geminicodeassist: Custom
Commands</code>.</p></li>
<li><p>In the <strong>Custom Commands</strong> box, select <strong>Add Item</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>In the <strong>Item</strong> field, enter <code translate="no" dir="ltr">add-comments</code> as the name of the command.</p></li>
<li><p>In the <strong>Value</strong> field, enter <code translate="no" dir="ltr">add comments to all functions without
comments in my code</code> as the prompt.</p></li>
<li><p>Click <strong>OK</strong>.</p></li>
</ol>

<p>You can now use the custom command <code translate="no" dir="ltr">add-comments</code> in your IDE. The command
appears in the list of commands in the Gemini Code Assist
Quick Pick menu (<kbd>Control+I</kbd> (for Windows and Linux) or
<kbd>Command+I</kbd> (for macOS)).</p></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_20" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><ol>
<li><p>In your IDE, navigate to <strong>Settings</strong> <span aria-label="and then">></span> <strong>Tools</strong> <span aria-label="and then">></span>
<strong>Gemini</strong> <span aria-label="and then">></span> <strong>Prompt Library</strong>.</p>

<p><img src="/static/gemini/images/intellij-prompt-library.png" alt="Prompt Library for IntelliJ Gemini Code Assist" class="screenshot"> </p></li>
<li><p>In the <strong>Prompt Library</strong> window, click
<span class="google-symbols" translate="no">add</span> <strong>Add</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>Name your custom command <code translate="no" dir="ltr">add-comments</code>.</p></li>
<li><p>In the Prompt Library&#39;s text box, enter the prompt:
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">Add comments to all functions without comments in this code</code>.</p></li>
<li><p>Select the <strong>Show in In-Editor Prompt</strong> checkbox if it&#39;s unselected.</p></li>
<li><p>Click <strong>OK</strong> to save the custom command in the Prompt Library.</p></li>
<li><p>In your code file, highlight the code that you want to modify.</p></li>
<li><p>Right-click the highlighted code and navigate to <strong>Gemini</strong> <span aria-label="and then">></span>
<strong>Prompt Library</strong> and then select the custom command <code translate="no" dir="ltr">add-comments</code>.</p>

<p>Gemini Code Assist executes the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">add-comments</code> command and
adds comments to your highlighted code.</p></li>
</ol>

<p>You can also invoke the custom command with the in-editor prompt by
performing the following tasks:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>In your code file, highlight the code that you want to modify, and press
<kbd>Alt+\</kbd> (for Windows and Linux) or <kbd>Cmd+\</kbd> (for macOS) to
open the <strong>Gemini Code Assist Quick Pick</strong> menu.</p></li>
<li><p>In the menu, select your custom command <code translate="no" dir="ltr">add-comments</code>.</p>

<p>Gemini Code Assist executes the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">add-comments</code> command and
adds comments to your highlighted code.</p></li>
</ol>

<p>In the Gemini Code Assist chat pane, you can type <kbd>@</kbd>
to retrieve and use a saved prompt in your Prompt Library.</p></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h2 id="create_rules" data-text="Create rules" tabindex="-1">Create rules</h2>

<p>You can create rules for Gemini Code Assist to follow, and the
rules are included in every chat prompt you enter.</p>

<p>Rules in Gemini let you define your preferences, such as:</p>

<ul>
<li>Coding style</li>
<li>Output formats</li>
<li>Tech stack</li>
<li>Language</li>
</ul>

<p>For example, you can create a rule such as &quot;Always give me concise responses in
Kotlin.&quot;</p>


<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_21" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><ol>
<li><p>In your code file, press <kbd>Control+I</kbd> (for Windows and Linux) or
<kbd>Command+I</kbd> (for macOS) to open the
<strong>Gemini Code Assist Quick Pick</strong> menu.</p></li>
<li><p>In the menu, search for and select <strong>Preferences: Open Settings (UI)</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>In the <strong>Search settings</strong> field, enter <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Geminicodeassist: Rules</code>.</p></li>
<li><p>In the text field, enter a rule such as: <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Always generate unit tests when
creating a new function</code>. You can also add one or more rules with multiple
lines in the text field.</p>

<p>After adding rules in the Rules settings,
Gemini Code Assist considers the rule for every prompt or
request you make.</p>

<p>To remove the rule, delete the content from the Rules text field.</p></li>
</ol></section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_21" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Rules aren&#39;t used in agent mode.</span></aside>
<ol>
<li>To create a rule, go to
<strong>Settings &gt; Tools &gt; Gemini &gt; Prompt Library &gt; Rules</strong> and then edit the
text in the editor.</li>
<li><p>To set the scope of the rule, in the <strong>Scope</strong> drop-down, select <strong>IDE</strong>
or <strong>Project</strong>.</p>

<ul>
<li>IDE-level rules are private to yourself and can be used across
multiple projects.</li>
<li>Project-level rules can be shared among teammates working on the same
project.</li>
</ul>

<p>To share prompts across the team you must add the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">.idea</code> folder to the
version control system.</p></li>
</ol>

<p>
<div style="text-align: center;">
  <img src="/static/gemini/images/intellij-rules.png" alt="Create Gemini rules in IntelliJ">
</div>
</p></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<h2 id="known_issues" data-text="Known issues" tabindex="-1">Known issues</h2>

<p>This section outlines the known issues of Gemini Code Assist:</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="vs-code_22" data-text=" VS Code " tabindex="-1"> VS Code </h3><ul>
<li><p><strong>Chat responses may be truncated when they include an updated version of a
large open file</strong></p>

<p>To work around this issue, select a smaller section of code and include an
additional directive in the chat prompt, such as <code translate="no" dir="ltr">only output the selected
code.</code></p></li>
<li><p><strong>Vim: Cannot accept or dismiss code generation suggestions unless in
insert mode</strong></p>

<p>When using the Vim plugin in normal mode, you can&#39;t accept or dismiss code
suggestions.</p>

<p>To work around this issue, press <kbd>i</kbd> to enter insert mode, and
then press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to accept the suggestion.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Vim: Inconsistent behavior when pressing <kbd>Esc</kbd> to dismiss
suggestions</strong></p>

<p>When you press <kbd>Esc</kbd>, both the IDE and
Gemini Code Assist suggestions are dismissed. This behavior
is different from the non-Vim behavior where pressing <kbd>Esc</kbd>
re-triggers Gemini Code Assist.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Sign-in attempts keep timing out</strong></p>

<p>If your sign-in attempts keep timing out, try adding the
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">cloudcode.beta.forceOobLogin</code> setting to your <code translate="no" dir="ltr">settings.json</code> file:</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="JSON"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">"cloudcode.beta.forceOobLogin"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kc">true</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code></li>
<li><p><strong>License recitation warnings don&#39;t persist across sessions</strong></p>

<p>If license recitation warnings don&#39;t persist across sessions, refer to the
persistent logs:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>Click <strong>View</strong> <span aria-label="and then">></span> <strong>Output</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>Select <strong>Gemini Code Assist - Citations</strong>.</p></li>
</ol></li>
<li><p><strong>Connectivity issues in the Gemini Code Assist output
window</strong></p>

<p>If you see a connection error or other connectivity problems in the
Gemini Code Assist output window, try the following:</p>

<ul>
<li><p>Configure your firewall to allow access to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">oauth2.googleapis.com</code> and
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">cloudaicompanion.googleapis.com</code>.</p></li>
<li><p>Configure your firewall to allow communication over HTTP/2, which gRPC
uses.</p></li>
</ul>

<p>You can use the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">grpc-health-probe</code> tool to test connectivity. A
successful check results in the following output:</p>

<p><code translate="no" dir="ltr">$ grpc-health-probe -addr cloudaicompanion.googleapis.com:443 -tls
error: this server does not implement the grpc health protocol
(grpc.health.v1.Health): GRPC target method can&#39;t be resolved</code></p>

<p>An unsuccessful check results in the following output:</p>

<p><code translate="no" dir="ltr">timeout: failed to connect service &quot;cloudaicompanion.googleapis.com:443&quot; within 1s</code></p>

<p>To obtain more details, run the following before <code translate="no" dir="ltr">grpc-health-probe</code>:</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded><code translate="no" dir="ltr">export GRPC_GO_LOG_SEVERITY_LEVEL=info
</code></pre></devsite-code></li>
</ul>

</section>
<section><h3 id="intellij_22" data-text=" IntelliJ " tabindex="-1"> IntelliJ </h3><p>There are no known issues for Gemini Code Assist for IntelliJ
and other supported JetBrains IDEs.</p></section>
</devsite-selector></div>

</ul>
